title: Basics of Bone and Mineral Metabolism

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: The skeletal system receives what share of total cardiac output?
questions.exp: The skeletal system is highly vascular — 10% of total cardiac output. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: Match cortical vs trabecular bone — 1) Cortical contribution  2) Trabecular contribution  3) Cortical unit  4) Trabecular unit … A) Trabeculae  B) 20%  C) 80%  D) Osteon
questions.exp: Cortical bone = 80% of mass, osteon unit; trabecular = 20%, trabeculae. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: Cortical bone is seen in ___ and trabecular bone in ___.
opts: Diaphysis of long bone; epiphysis and vertebrae
questions.exp: Cortical in diaphysis of long bones; trabecular in epiphysis and vertebrae. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: ‘The Haversian system is present in cortical bone but absent in trabecular bone.’
questions.exp: Haversian system (+) cortical, (−) trabecular. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: Match hormone action on bone type — 1) Cortical bone  2) Trabecular bone … A) Steroid hormones  B) PTH and thyroid
questions.exp: PTH and thyroid act on cortical bone; steroid hormones on trabecular bone. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: Trabecular bone has a HIGH remodelling rate because of:
questions.exp: High remodelling/bone turnover d/t ↑ surface area to mass ratio; also high metabolic activity and porosity. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: Osteoporosis is evaluated on trabecular bone using:
opts: Bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular bone score (TBS)
questions.exp: BMD plus the newer trabecular bone score (TBS). (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863
questions.q: Two patients have near-identical BMD (L1–L4 ≈ 0.99) but TBS 1.432 vs 1.124. The patient with TBS 1.124 has:
opts: Degraded micro-architecture → osteoporosis despite similar BMD
questions.exp: Normal TBS (1.432) = good micro-architecture; low TBS (1.124) = degraded micro-architecture → osteoporosis. (Book p863)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: Cells contribute what percentage of bone, with matrix making the rest?
questions.exp: Cells 2% (osteoblasts, osteoclasts, osteocytes); matrix 98%. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: Match matrix fraction — 1) Organic  2) Inorganic … A) Calcium, phosphorous, magnesium (60–70%)  B) Type I collagen + non-collagenous proteins (30–40%)
questions.exp: Organic 30–40% (type I collagen predominant); inorganic 60–70% (Ca, P, Mg). (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: The predominant organic constituent of bone matrix is:
questions.exp: Type I collagen is predominant among organic constituents. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: Matrix GLA protein functions as an inhibitor of vascular calcification; it is inhibited by:
questions.exp: Matrix GLA protein inhibits vascular calcification; warfarin (vit K antagonist) inhibits it → precipitates calcification. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: The non-collagenous proteins listed are osteopontin, osteocalcin, thrombospondin, matrix GLA protein, fibronectin and:
questions.exp: The sixth listed non-collagenous protein is proteoglycans. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: Match collagen type to disorder — 1) Type I  2) Type III  3) Type IV  4) Type VII … A) EDS type IV (vascular)  B) Epidermolysis bullosa  C) Osteogenesis imperfecta  D) Alport/Goodpasture
questions.exp: Type I → OI (also EDS VII/arthrochalasia, osteoporosis); type III → EDS IV vascular; type IV → Alport/Goodpasture; type VII → epidermolysis bullosa. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: Type II collagen is distributed in cartilage and vitreous humor; its disorder association is:
questions.exp: Type II (cartilage, vitreous humor) → chondrodysplasia. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: Which collagen type is NOT linked to a named disorder in the table?
questions.exp: Type 8 (endothelium) has no listed disorder (−). (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864
questions.q: EDS classical type is associated with which minor collagen?
questions.exp: Type 5 (minor) → EDS classical type. (Book p864)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: The bone mineral is formed as ___ from the amorphous calcium phosphate precursor.
questions.exp: Amorphous calcium phosphate (precursor) → calcium hydroxy apatite (bone). (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: In the OLD hypothesis, mineralisation at the metaphyseal end is driven by which enzymes?
questions.exp: Old hypothesis: osteoblast lays matrix (type I collagen) then mineralisation by ALP, annexin, 5'-nucleotidase; osteoblast → osteocyte. (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: Alkaline phosphatase promotes mineralisation by:
questions.exp: ALP hydrolyses inhibitors of mineralisation; ↑ mineralisation → ↑ ALP. (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: ‘Serum ALP is NOT raised in multiple myeloma because mineralisation is decreased there.’
opts: False — ALP is high in myeloma
questions.exp: ALP is not ↑ in multiple myeloma as mineralisation is ↓. (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: The sources of ALP listed are:
questions.exp: Sources of ALP: bone, kidney, placenta. (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: The NEW hypothesis of bone formation states that:
opts: Osteoblast converts to osteocyte, and the osteocyte lays down matrix and mineralises it
questions.exp: New hypothesis: osteoblast → osteocyte; osteocyte lays down matrix → mineralisation (bone added outside-to-inside by osteocytes). (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: Which enzyme has ONLY a liver source and helps confirm the hepatic origin of a raised ALP?
questions.exp: GGT is only liver source and confirms hepatic origin of ↑ALP; ALP and 5'-nucleotidase are not specific (other sources). (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865
questions.q: Which is NOT a cholestatic liver enzyme in the note?
questions.exp: Cholestatic liver enzymes: ALP, 5'-nucleotidase (not specific), GGT (liver-only) — not ALT. (Book p865)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: Osteoblasts arise from:
questions.exp: Osteoblasts are of mesenchymal origin. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: Match bone formation route — 1) Mesenchymal → chondroblast  2) Mesenchymal → osteoblast via RUNX2 … A) Intramembranous (skull bones, clavicle)  B) Endochondral bone formation
questions.exp: Chondroblasts → endochondral; RUNX2-driven osteoblasts → intramembranous (skull, clavicle). (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: The transcription factor driving osteoblast differentiation (intramembranous) is:
questions.exp: RUNX2 (transcription factor); its defect causes cleido-cranial dysplasia. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: A RUNX2 defect causes:
questions.exp: RUNX2 defect → cleido-cranial dysplasia. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: The osteocyte is described as the:
opts: Master regulator of bone formation and resorption
questions.exp: Osteocyte = master regulator of bone formation & resorption; mechanoreceptor for loading/unloading and estrogen. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: Estrogen reduces osteoclast numbers by:
questions.exp: Estrogen kills osteoclasts → ↓ osteoclast numbers (at the level of the joint). (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: Unloading forces or estrogen deficiency make osteocytes secrete:
questions.exp: Osteocytes produce sclerostin under unloading/estrogen deficiency. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: Match sclerostin actions — 1) Inhibits WNT1  2) Activates osteoclast … A) ↑ bone resorption  B) Inhibits osteoblast differentiation from mesenchymal stem cells
questions.exp: Sclerostin inhibits WNT1 (osteoblast formation/action) → blocks osteoblast differentiation, and activates osteoclasts. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: FGF23 produced by osteocytes is the most potent:
questions.exp: FGF23 inhibits phosphorus reabsorption at PCT → phosphaturic (most potent). (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: Osteoclasts are of ___ origin and use ___ to generate protons for resorption.
questions.exp: Osteoclasts: macrophage origin; carbonic anhydrase type 2 generates protons → bone resorption with irregular Howship lacunae. (Book p866)

questions.sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866
questions.q: The irregular resorption pits made by osteoclasts are called ___.
questions.exp: Irregular activity produces Howship lacunae. (Book p866)

questions.sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867
questions.q: On the osteoblast surface, PTH and vitamin D upregulate RANKL, which binds ___ on pre-osteoclasts (with M-CSF) to activate osteoclasts.
questions.exp: RANKL (from osteoblasts) binds RANK on preosteoclasts with M-CSF → active osteoclast (acid secretion, lysosome, ruffled membrane). (Book p867)

questions.sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867
questions.q: OPG (osteoprotegerin) acts by:
opts: Physiological inhibition of the RANK–RANKL interaction
questions.exp: OPG physiologically inhibits RANK–RANKL interaction. (Book p867)

questions.sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867
questions.q: Calcitonin binds receptors on the basal surface of osteoclasts to:
questions.exp: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast → inhibits bone resorption. (Book p867)

questions.sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867
questions.q: Calcitonin is used to treat hypercalcaemia because it also:
questions.exp: It stimulates renal calcium clearance causing hypocalcaemia, hence used in hypercalcaemia. (Book p867)

questions.sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867
questions.q: Match the bone cycle steps to duration — 1) Osteoclast activation + bone resorption  2) Reversal + bone formation + mineralisation … A) 3 months  B) 3 weeks
questions.exp: Resorption phase (steps 1–2) ~3 weeks; reversal/formation/mineralisation (3–5) ~3 months. (Book p867)

questions.sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867
questions.q: The correct order of the bone remodelling cycle is:
opts: Osteoclast activation → resorption → reversal → formation → mineralisation
questions.exp: Steps: 1 osteoclast activation, 2 bone resorption, 3 reversal, 4 bone formation, 5 mineralisation. (Book p867)

questions.sec: Bone turnover markers and vitamin D mechanism · p868
questions.q: Match marker to category — 1) TRAP  2) CTP  3) NTX  4) Osteocalcin … A) Formation  B) Resorption
questions.exp: Resorption markers: TRAP, CTP, NTX; formation: total/bone ALP, osteocalcin, PICP, PINP. (Book p868)

questions.sec: Bone turnover markers and vitamin D mechanism · p868
questions.q: Which is a bone FORMATION marker (odd one out among resorption markers)?
questions.exp: bsALP is a formation marker; TRAP, CTP, NTX are resorption markers. (Book p868)

questions.sec: Bone turnover markers and vitamin D mechanism · p868
questions.q: The formation markers PICP and PINP are propeptides of:
questions.exp: PICP/PINP = C- and N-terminal propeptides of procollagen type I. (Book p868)

questions.sec: Bone turnover markers and vitamin D mechanism · p868
questions.q: Vitamin D is a Group I hormone acting via:
questions.exp: Group I hormone with intracellular receptor in nucleus — heterodimer receptor type 2. (Book p868)

questions.sec: Bone turnover markers and vitamin D mechanism · p868
questions.q: Match the vitamin D receptor complex — 1) Activated VDR partner  2) DNA element bound … A) VDRE  B) RXR
questions.exp: 1,25-OH vit D activates VDR which heterodimerizes with RXR and binds VDRE to drive gene transcription. (Book p868)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: The plant source of vitamin D is:
questions.exp: Plant source = ergocalciferol; animal/skin/diet = cholecalciferol (vit D3). (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: The liver enzyme converting cholecalciferol to calcidiol is:
questions.exp: Liver vit D3 25-hydroxylase makes calcidiol/25-OH D3. (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: The form used to MEASURE blood vitamin D levels (long t½, major circulating/storage form) is:
questions.exp: Calcidiol has long t½, is the major circulating & storage form, and is used to measure vit D levels. (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: The inactive shunt product formed by 24-α-hydroxylase is:
questions.exp: 24-α-hydroxylase yields 24,25(OH)2 D3 (inactive form). (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: The renal (PCT) enzyme making the ACTIVE form, stimulated by PTH, is:
questions.exp: Kidney PCT 1α-hydroxylase (activated by PTH) makes 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol/calcitriol (active). (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: Calcitriol in intestinal epithelium induces which trio to absorb calcium?
opts: TRPV5/6 channels alone at the membrane
Calcium-binding protein, calcium-stimulated ATPase, alkaline phosphatase
questions.exp: It induces calcium-binding protein, calcium-stimulated ATPase and alkaline phosphatase → intestinal Ca absorption → raises plasma Ca, inhibiting PTH. (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: Match drug to vitamin D effect — 1) Phenytoin  2) INH  3) Steroids & ketoconazole … A) Inhibits 25-hydroxylase  B) Causes vit D resistance  C) Inhibit 1α-hydroxylase
questions.exp: Phenytoin causes vit D resistance; INH inhibits 25-hydroxylase; steroids & ketoconazole inhibit 1α-hydroxylase. (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869
questions.q: ‘In nephrotic syndrome, vitamin D binding globulin is lost in urine while the vitamin D level stays normal.’
questions.exp: Vit D binding globulin is lost in urine in nephrotic syndrome (vit D level normal). (Book p869)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: Vitamin D increases Ca2+ absorption predominantly in the:
questions.exp: ↑ Ca2+ absorption predominantly in jejunum (TRPV5/6, calbindin-D, NCX1, PMCA1b). (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: VDR has anti-proliferative (protective against malignancy) effects on:
questions.exp: VDR anti-proliferative on skin, breast, prostate — vit D protective against malignancies. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: PTH is an ___ amino-acid molecule; its related peptide (PTHrP) has ___ aa.
questions.exp: PTH = 84 aa; PTH-related peptide = 139 aa. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: The bioactive form of PTH comprises the:
questions.exp: Bioactive form = first 34 aa. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: PTH's short half-life is:
questions.exp: t½ 2–4 min, so the sample must be collected and transported via cold chain. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: Intact PTH is measured using:
questions.exp: 2nd generation assays (double antibody IRMA / two-site binding) measure intact PTH; normal 50–100 pg/mL. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: The normal intact PTH value is:
questions.exp: Normal intact PTH 50–100 pg/mL. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Vitamin D action in jejunum, anti-proliferative effect and PTH basics · p870
questions.q: The overall effect of PTH on calcium and phosphorus is:
questions.exp: Overall: ↑ Ca2+, ↓ P. (Book p870)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: Match parathyroid development — 1) 3rd pharyngeal pouch  2) 4th pharyngeal pouch … A) Superior parathyroid  B) Inferior parathyroid (ectopic intrathyroid m/c)
questions.exp: 3rd pouch → inferior parathyroid (ectopic, intrathyroid m/c); 4th pouch → superior parathyroid; endodermal origin at 5–7 weeks. (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: A Tbx1 defect causes:
questions.exp: Tbx1 defect → Di George syndrome (22q microdeletion). (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: A GATA3 defect produces the triad of:
opts: Hypoparathyroidism, sensorineural hearing loss, renal dysfunction
questions.exp: GATA3 defect → hypoparathyroidism, SNHL, renal dysfunction. (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: GCMB and SOX3 defects lead to:
questions.exp: GCMB & SOX3 defect → hypoparathyroidism. (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: The parathyroid cell with abundant mitochondria and affinity for 99mTc-sestamibi is the:
questions.exp: Oxyntic cells contain large mitochondria and take up 99mTc-sestamibi. (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: A sestamibi scan shows a hot parathyroid focus. The applied principle is that adenoma has:
questions.exp: Adenoma → ↑ oxyntic cells → ↑ uptake of 99mTc-sestamibi (taken up by oxyntic cells). (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: Match the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop — 1) FGF23 on Vit D & PTH  2) PTH on Vit D & FGF23  3) Vit D on PTH & FGF23 … A) (+) Vit D, (+) FGF23  B) (−) PTH, (+) FGF23  C) (−) Vit D, (−) PTH
questions.exp: FGF23 inhibits Vit D and PTH; PTH stimulates Vit D and FGF23; Vit D inhibits PTH and stimulates FGF23. (Book p871)

questions.sec: Parathyroid anatomy, transcription factors and the PTH–VitD–FGF23 loop · p871
questions.q: PTH stimulates vitamin D by activating:
questions.exp: PTH (+) 1α-hydroxylase → stimulates Vit D; Vit D (−) parathyroid proliferation → inhibits PTH. (Book p871)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: FGF23 is beneficial because of P excretion but harmful because it:
questions.exp: FGF23 harmful as it (−) vit D; beneficial d/t P excretion. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: Match FGF23 actions — 1) Na-P cotransporter type 2a (PCT)  2) 1α-hydroxylase  3) PTH … A) (−) via Klotho receptor (lost in CKD d/t Klotho resistance)  B) (−) → ↓ vit D  C) (−) → phosphaturic
questions.exp: FGF23 inhibits the Na-P cotransporter (phosphaturic), 1α-hydroxylase (↓vit D) and PTH via Klotho (not seen in CKD due to Klotho resistance). (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: Match PTH vs vitamin D on the kidney — 1) PTH  2) Vitamin D … A) ↓ Ca/P excretion (by 25(OH)D3 & 1,25(OH)2D3)  B) ↑ Ca reabsorption and ↑ P excretion
questions.exp: PTH ↑ Ca reabsorption & ↑ P excretion; vit D ↓ Ca/P excretion. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: On bone, intermittent LOW doses of PTH cause:
questions.exp: PTH normally ↑ resorption (mobilises Ca); intermittent low doses ↑ bone formation. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: Match vitamin D metabolite to bone effect — 1) 1,25(OH)2 D3  2) 24,25(OH)2 D3 … A) ↑ bone formation  B) ↑ bone resorption
questions.exp: 1,25(OH)2D3 ↑ resorption; 24,25(OH)2D3 ↑ formation. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: By the Endocrine Society of India, a vitamin D level <12 ng/ml (deficient) is treated with:
opts: 50,000 IU per week for 6–8 weeks, maintenance 600–2000 IU/day
questions.exp: Deficient: 50000 IU/week ×6–8 wks, maintenance 600–2000 IU/day. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: Vitamin D insufficiency (12–19 ng/ml) is managed with at least:
questions.exp: Insufficient: ≥400 IU/day; >20 ng/ml = sufficient. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: The RDA of vitamin D is 600 IU till 70 years and ___ after 70 years.
questions.exp: RDA 600 IU till 70 yrs; 800 IU after 70 yrs. (Book p872)

questions.sec: FGF23 actions, PTH vs vitamin D table and vitamin D assay · p872
questions.q: When hydroxylation is impaired, the active drug and maintenance dose are:
opts: Calcitriol 0.25–0.5 µg/day; maintenance 0.25 µg every alternate day
questions.exp: Hydroxylation impaired → calcitriol 0.25–0.5 µg/day; maintenance 0.25 µg alternate day. (Book p872)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: Adverse effects of PTH on the CVS include:
questions.exp: CVS adverse effects: medial calcification, atherosclerosis, HTN. (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: PTH receptors signal through:
questions.exp: PTH receptors are GPCR (cAMP/PKA). (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: The PTH receptor type on which PTHrP also acts, mediating paraneoplastic hypercalcaemia (squamous cell carcinoma of head & neck, lung), is:
questions.exp: Type 1 receptor: PTHrp also acts here → paraneoplastic role (SCC head & neck, lung). (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: ‘A fall in ionised calcium is the MORE sensitive stimulus, inhibiting CaSR and raising PTH; a rise activates CaSR and lowers PTH.’
opts: False — CaSR is in the kidney only
True, but only with high phosphate

questions.q: The most important regulator of PTH is:
questions.exp: Ionised Ca2+ is the most important regulator; basal PTH secretion is always present. (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: ‘Phosphate deficiency impairs PTH release.’
questions.exp: Deficiency of P impairs PTH release. (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: Match CaSR mutation — 1) Loss of function  2) Gain of function … A) Bartter syndrome type 5  B) Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia
questions.exp: CaSR loss-of-function → familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia; gain-of-function → Bartter syndrome type 5. (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: Senile osteoporosis arises because mesenchymal stem cells differentiate into:
questions.exp: Senile osteoporosis: mesenchymal stem cells → adipocyte instead of osteoblast. (Book p873)

questions.sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873
questions.q: ___ helps in Ca2+ reabsorption from the kidney.
questions.exp: Claudin 16 helps in Ca2+ reabsorption from kidney. (Book p873)

units.title: Bone types, constituents and the collagen table
units.guide: Skeleton 10% cardiac output. Cortical 80% (diaphysis, osteon, Haversian +, PTH/thyroid, low turnover) vs trabecular 20% (epiphysis/vertebrae, trabeculae, steroids, high turnover d/t surface:mass); osteoporosis judged on trabecular bone via BMD + TBS (normal 1.432 good; low 1.124 degraded). Constituents: cells 2%, matrix 98% (organic 30–40% type I collagen + osteopontin/osteocalcin/thrombospondin/matrix GLA (warfarin-inhibited → calcification)/fibronectin/proteoglycans; inorganic 60–70% Ca/P/Mg). Collagen disorders: I OI/EDS VII; V EDS classical; II chondrodysplasia; III EDS IV; IV Alport/Goodpasture; VII epidermolysis bullosa; VIII none.

units.title: Bone formation hypotheses, ALP and the bone cells
units.guide: Amorphous Ca phosphate → hydroxyapatite. Old: osteoblast lays type I matrix, mineralised by ALP/annexin/5'-nucleotidase; new: osteoblast → osteocyte lays matrix. ALP hydrolyses mineralisation inhibitors; not ↑ in myeloma; sources bone/kidney/placenta; GGT liver-only confirms hepatic ALP. Osteoblast mesenchymal (RUNX2 → intramembranous skull/clavicle; defect cleidocranial dysplasia). Osteocyte master regulator, mechanoreceptor, estrogen kills osteoclasts; sclerostin (unloading/estrogen deficiency) inhibits WNT1 + activates osteoclasts; FGF23 most potent phosphaturic. Osteoclast macrophage origin, CA type 2 protons, Howship lacunae.

units.title: RANKL/OPG, calcitonin, bone cycle and turnover markers
units.guide: PTH/vit D ↑ RANKL on osteoblasts → RANK + M-CSF activates osteoclast; OPG inhibits RANK–RANKL. Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast + renal Ca clearance → hypocalcaemia (Rx hypercalcaemia). Cycle: activation → resorption (3 wks) → reversal → formation → mineralisation (3 months). Resorption markers TRAP/CTP/NTX; formation total & bone ALP, osteocalcin, PICP, PINP. Vit D = Group I nuclear heterodimer (type 2), VDR+RXR on VDRE.

units.title: Vitamin D metabolism, jejunal action and PTH basics
units.guide: D3 (animal/skin) vs ergocalciferol (plant); liver 25-hydroxylase → calcidiol (long t½, storage, assay form); 24-α-hydroxylase → inactive 24,25; renal PCT 1α-hydroxylase (PTH-stimulated) → calcitriol → intestinal Ca-binding protein/Ca-ATPase/ALP → ↑Ca → inhibits PTH. Drugs: phenytoin resistance, INH inhibits 25-hydroxylase, steroids/ketoconazole inhibit 1α. Nephrotic: DBP lost, vit D normal. Jejunum TRPV5/6-calbindin-NCX1-PMCA1b; VDR anti-proliferative (skin/breast/prostate). PTH 84 aa (PTHrP 139), bioactive 1-34, t½ 2-4 min (cold chain), 2nd-gen assay 50-100 pg/mL, ↑Ca ↓P.

units.title: Parathyroid anatomy and the PTH–vitD–FGF23 axis
units.guide: Endodermal, 5-7 wks: 3rd pouch → inferior (ectopic intrathyroid m/c), 4th → superior. TFs: Tbx1 → DiGeorge (22q); GATA3 → hypoPT+SNHL+renal; GCMB/SOX3 → hypoPT. Oxyntic cells (mitochondria, sestamibi). Loop: FGF23 (−)vitD (−)PTH; PTH (+)vitD (+)FGF23; vitD (−)PTH (+)FGF23; PTH via 1α-hydroxylase. FGF23: (−)Na-P 2a phosphaturic, (−)1α, (−)PTH via Klotho (CKD resistance). PTH kidney ↑Ca ↑P-excretion; vit D ↓excretion; bone PTH resorption (intermittent low dose formation); vitD 1,25 resorption / 24,25 formation. Assay: <12 deficient 50k IU/wk ×6-8 + 600-2000/day; 12-19 ≥400/day; >20 sufficient; RDA 600/800; hydroxylation impaired calcitriol 0.25-0.5 µg.

units.title: PTH receptors, sigmoid rule, CaSR mutations and senile osteoporosis
units.guide: CVS: medial calcification, atherosclerosis, HTN. GPCR cAMP/PKA; type 1 receptor also binds PTHrP (SCC head-neck/lung paraneoplastic). Sigmoid: ↑Ca activates CaSR → ↓PTH; ↓Ca (more sensitive) → ↑PTH; ionised Ca most important; P deficiency impairs release. CaSR loss → FHH; gain → Bartter type 5. Senile osteoporosis MSC → adipocyte; claudin 16 renal Ca reabsorption.
